It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Interactive Volume Illustration](5272-interactive-volume-illustration-hatching.md) by explicitly modeling paint layer accumulation through a 2D height field rather than relying solely on surface normals or simple shading [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the technique simulates paint undulations and overlap shadows using a '2D height field' generated from stroke height maps and overlap counts. It further clarifies that this approach is used to 'avoid rendering expensive three-dimensional mesh models' and relies on calculating 'per-pixel normals using directional derivatives of the height field' for Phong shading, rather than relying on simple surface normals of a 3D mesh or simple shading alone. This aligns with the claim that it models paint layer accumulation through a 2D height field rather than relying solely on surface normals or simple shading.

**Inputs:** A list of strokes, where each stroke has an associated color, opacity map, and height map [S1].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly supports this: 1) It mentions creating a 'list of strokes' (VC algorithm section). 2) It describes a 'Color Pass' where strokes are 'colored and textured with an opacity map' (implying color and opacity map are associated inputs). 3) It describes a 'Height Pass' where strokes are textured with a 'height map paired with the opacity map' (implying height map is an associated input). 4) The notes explicitly state 'Draw each stroke colored... textured with an opacity map' and 'Draw each stroke white and textured with the height map paired with the opacity map', confirming these attributes are part of the stroke definition used in the rendering pipeline.
